# Model and source

Thorsted 2023 fitted one model simultaneously to digitized in vitro and in
vivo data. The library carries it as two files, one per experimental system,
because no experiment spans both systems and the two arms differ in their
states, inputs and several parameter values:

```{r model-load}
ui_vitro <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thorsted_2023_neutrophil_invitro"))
ui_mouse <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thorsted_2023_neutrophil_mouse"))
```

* Citation: `r ui_vitro$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13046>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10725272/>
* Supplements: Data S2 (the final NONMEM control stream) and Table S1 (the
  digitized NONMEM data file), linked from the article landing page.

* In vitro arm: `r ui_vitro$description`
* Mouse arm: `r ui_mouse$description`

# Population

The model was built on published data, digitized from figures. Seven in vitro
studies (Table 1, In vitro-1 to In vitro-7) incubated human neutrophils at a
fixed concentration of 0 to 1 x 10^7 cells/mL with *Staphylococcus
epidermidis*, *S. aureus*, *Escherichia coli*, *Streptococcus pyogenes* or
*Corynebacterium* at inocula of 10^3 to 10^10 CFU/mL. The incubations ran for
1 to 3 h at 37 C in at least 5% human serum, in suspension or in fibrin gel.
The studies measured total viable, extracellular or intracellular CFU. One
study (In vitro-7) was held back for external evaluation. Together they give
115 experiments with 403 CFU observations.

Five mouse studies (Table 1, Mice-1 to Mice-5) supplied the in vivo data.
Four described *Acinetobacter baumannii* pneumonia in C57BL/6 or
Swiss-Webster mice. Mice-2 pretreated the animals with intraperitoneal
cyclophosphamide 96 and 24 h before inoculation (50/50, 100/50 or
200/150 mg/kg, or vehicle). The fifth study measured steady-state blood and
lung neutrophils in uninfected mice. Together they give 21 experiments with
56 CFU, 5 blood-neutrophil and 16 lung-neutrophil observations. Lung counts
were converted to per-gram units with a lung weight of 0.175 g.

No between-experiment variability was estimated (`$OMEGA 0 FIX` in Data S2),
so both models are deterministic and every simulation below is a typical-value
simulation.

```{r population}
str(ui_vitro$population, max.level = 1)
str(ui_mouse$population, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them. All estimates are from the "Final model" column of
Table 2.

| Parameter | In vitro | Mouse | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kgrowth` (1/h) | 1.84 | 0.502 | Table 2, bacterial growth, in vitro and in vivo rows |
| `kdeath` (1/h) | 0.179 fixed | 0.179 fixed | Table 2 (from Nielsen 2007) |
| `klag` (1/h) | 0.290 | -- | Table 2; bacteria start in the growing state in vivo |
| `Bmax` (CFU/mL or CFU/g) | 2.5 x 10^9 fixed | 2.5 x 10^9 fixed | Table 2; Data S2 shares `BMAX` |
| `kN,max` (1/h) | 8.85 | 0.820 | Table 2; shared by phagocytosis and digestion |
| `kN,loss` (1/h) | 0.779 | 0 fixed | Table 2 |
| `N50,dig` (cells/mL) | 6.55 x 10^6 | 6.55 x 10^6 | Table 2 |
| `N50,phag` (cells/mL) | 1.19 x 10^6 | 1.19 x 10^6 | Table 2 |
| `P/N50` (CFU/cell) | 3.41 | 3.41 | Table 2; shared by phagocytosis and digestion |
| `kM,kill` (1/h) | -- | 0.287 | Table 2 |
| `kM,loss` (1/h) | -- | 0.0111 | Table 2 |
| `ka`, `CL`, `V` (cyclophosphamide) | -- | 20.9 1/h, 0.311 mL/h, 0.153 mL | Table 2 ("Scaled"); Data S2 `$PK` scaling expressions |
| `MTT` (h) | -- | 37.7 | Table 2 ("Scaled"); Data S2 `52.8 * (0.025/0.295)**0.136` |
| `gamma` | -- | 0.149 fixed | Table 2 |
| `DSLP` (mL/mg) | -- | 1.26 | Table 2 |
| `Ncirc,T0` (cells/mL) | -- | 1.69 x 10^6 | Table 2 |
| `NAMP`, `NT0`, `NSW` | -- | 44.2, 50.5 h, 28.2 h | Table 2 |
| Lung weight (g) | -- | 0.175 fixed | Data S2 `THETA(15)`; Materials and Methods |
| Residual SD, CFU (log10) | 0.279 | 0.600 | Table 2 (SD scale) |
| Residual SD, neutrophils (log10) | -- | 0.161 | Table 2 (SD scale) |

| Equation | Implementation | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Bacterial lag / growing / resting states | `bact_lag`, `bact_susceptible`, `bact_resting` | Equations 1-3; `kSR` defined in the text above Equation 1 |
| Phagocytosis and digestion rates | `kn_phag`, `kn_dig` | Equations 4-5 |
| Phagocytosed bacteria | `bact_phagocytosed` | Equation 6 |
| Cyclophosphamide PK | `depot`, `central` | Equations 7-8 |
| Myelosuppression chain | `prol`, `transit1`-`transit3`, `circ` | Equations 9-13 |
| Lung neutrophil influx and surge | `neut_lung` | Equation 14 |
| Additional in vivo phagocytic capacity | `bact_phagocytosed_mac` | Results; Data S2 `$DES` (`KPGM`, `KDGM`, `MACRF`) |
| Observations | `log_cfu`, `log_cfu_extracellular`, `log_cfu_intracellular`, `log_anc`, `log_neut_lung` | Data S2 `$ERROR` |

# Reproducing the published fit on the deposited data

Table S1 is the NONMEM data file the authors fitted. The chunk below embeds the
dose and observation records of In vitro-2 and of all five mouse studies,
copied from Table S1. Baseline observations (`T0DATA = 1`) are dropped, as the
authors' `IGNORE` did, and so are the macrophage records (`LOCA` 6 and 8).
`CMT` and `LOCA` keep their Data S2 meanings: doses to compartment 1
(neutrophils), 2 (bacteria, lag state), 3 (bacteria, growing state) and 12
(cyclophosphamide). The observations are 1 (intracellular CFU),
2 (extracellular CFU), 3 and 4 (total CFU), 5 (blood neutrophils) and
7 (lung neutrophils).

Neither model has random effects. The residual SD that maximises the
likelihood at the published fixed effects is then the root-mean-square residual
of the typical-value predictions. So a correct implementation should give
root-mean-square residuals close to the Table 2 SDs.

```{r s1-solve}
cmt_vitro <- c(`1` = "neut_tube", `2` = "bact_lag", `3` = "bact_susceptible", `5` = "bact_phagocytosed")
cmt_mouse <- c(`3` = "bact_susceptible", `12` = "depot")
out_name <- c(`1` = "log_cfu_intracellular", `2` = "log_cfu_extracellular",
              `3` = "log_cfu", `4` = "log_cfu", `5` = "log_anc", `7` = "log_neut_lung")

# Typical-value predictions for every observation record of the given IDs.
predict_s1 <- function(ui, ids, cmt_map) {
  dose <- s1_dose[s1_dose$ID %in% ids, ]
  obs <- s1_obs[s1_obs$ID %in% ids, ]
  ev <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = dose$ID, time = dose$TIME, amt = dose$AMT, evid = 1L,
               cmt = unname(cmt_map[as.character(dose$CMT)]), dvid = NA_integer_),
    distinct(obs, id = ID, time = TIME) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(ev$cmt[ev$evid == 1L]))
  # Single-threaded throughout this article: with several threads, rxode2
  # 5.1.8 intermittently carried a cyclophosphamide effect into an untreated
  # subject of this event table.
  sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev, returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L,
                                       omega = NA, sigma = NA, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10))
  obs |>
    rowwise() |>
    mutate(PRED = sim[[out_name[[as.character(LOCA)]]]][sim$id == ID & sim$time == TIME][1]) |>
    ungroup()
}

pred <- bind_rows(
  predict_s1(ui_vitro, unique(s1_obs$ID[s1_obs$STUD < 99]), cmt_vitro),
  predict_s1(ui_mouse, unique(s1_obs$ID[s1_obs$STUD > 99]), cmt_mouse)
) |>
  mutate(
    endpoint = case_when(
      STUD < 99 ~ "In vitro-2 total CFU",
      LOCA == 4 & STUD == 230 ~ "Mice-4 lung CFU",
      LOCA == 4 ~ "Mice-1, -2, -3 lung CFU",
      TRUE ~ "Blood and lung neutrophils"
    ),
    res = DV - PRED
  )
stopifnot(!anyNA(pred$PRED))

rmse <- pred |>
  group_by(endpoint) |>
  summarise(n = n(), rmse = sqrt(mean(res^2)), mean_residual = mean(res), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(table2_sd = c(`Blood and lung neutrophils` = 0.161, `In vitro-2 total CFU` = 0.279,
                       `Mice-1, -2, -3 lung CFU` = 0.600, `Mice-4 lung CFU` = 0.600)[endpoint])
rmse |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint, "Records" = n, "RMS residual (log10)" = rmse,
    "Mean residual (log10)" = mean_residual, "Table 2 SD (log10)" = table2_sd
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The neutrophil endpoints (`r round(rmse$rmse[rmse$endpoint == "Blood and lung neutrophils"], 3)`
against 0.161) and the lung CFU of Mice-1 to Mice-3
(`r round(rmse$rmse[rmse$endpoint == "Mice-1, -2, -3 lung CFU"], 3)` against 0.600)
reproduce the published residual SDs. The in vitro residual SD (0.279) pools six
studies. In vitro-2, the one study embedded here, sits a little below it.
Over all six in vitro studies, the maintainers' check of the full Table S1
gave a root-mean-square residual of 0.279.

Mice-4 is the exception. Data S2 gives that study its own in vivo
growth-rate multiplier (`IF(STUD==230) KGR = THETA(1) * THETA(25)`), but
Table 2 reports no value for it. This model applies the common in vivo
`kgrowth` to every study, so the three Mice-4 CFU records are over-predicted by
about 2 log10 units. The Mice-4 lung-neutrophil records do not depend on
`kgrowth` and are fitted well.

```{r s1-check}
stopifnot(
  # Exact structural agreement: no random effects, so the RMS residual equals
  # the ML residual SD at the published fixed effects.
  abs(rmse$rmse[rmse$endpoint == "Blood and lung neutrophils"] / 0.161 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(rmse$rmse[rmse$endpoint == "Mice-1, -2, -3 lung CFU"] / 0.600 - 1) < 0.05,
  rmse$rmse[rmse$endpoint == "In vitro-2 total CFU"] < 0.279,
  # Mice-4 carries an unreported study-specific growth multiplier.
  rmse$mean_residual[rmse$endpoint == "Mice-4 lung CFU"] < -1
)
```

```{r s1-plot, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(pred, aes(PRED, DV, colour = endpoint)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Typical-value prediction (log10)", y = "Digitized observation (log10)",
       colour = NULL,
       title = "Observations from Table S1 against predictions from the packaged models") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# In vitro behaviour

## Growth controls and killing at fixed neutrophil concentrations

This chunk follows the In vitro-1 design (Table 1): inocula of 10^5 and
10^7 CFU/mL with 0 to 4 x 10^6 neutrophils/mL, followed for 1.5 h. Bacteria are
dosed into `bact_lag` and neutrophils into `neut_tube`, both at time 0 and in
concentration units.

```{r invitro-design}
# One row per experiment: inoculum (CFU/mL) and neutrophil concentration (cells/mL).
invitro_events <- function(design, times) {
  design$id <- seq_len(nrow(design))
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = design$id, time = 0, amt = design$inoc, evid = 1L,
               cmt = "bact_lag", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = design$id[design$neut > 0], time = 0,
               amt = design$neut[design$neut > 0], evid = 1L,
               cmt = "neut_tube", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = design$id, time = times) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

design1 <- tidyr::expand_grid(inoc = c(1e5, 1e7), neut = c(0, 4e5, 1e6, 4e6))
sim1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_vitro, invitro_events(design1, seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.05)),
                        returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L, omega = NA, sigma = NA) |>
  left_join(mutate(design1, id = row_number()), by = "id")
```

```{r invitro-plot}
ggplot(sim1, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = factor(neut))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Inoculum", format(inoc, scientific = TRUE), "CFU/mL")) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Total viable bacteria (log10 CFU/mL)",
       colour = "Neutrophils\n(cells/mL)",
       title = "In vitro total viable CFU (design of In vitro-1)",
       caption = "Compare with the In vitro-1 panels of Figure 2a of Thorsted 2023.") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Digestion of phagocytosed bacteria

The two digestion studies started from bacteria that were already inside
neutrophils, and in Table S1 their inoculum is dosed straight into the
phagocytosed compartment. This chunk does the same: 8.91 x 10^5 CFU/mL into
`bact_phagocytosed` with 5 x 10^6 neutrophils/mL, which is experiment 114 of
Table S1. It reads the intracellular output.

```{r digestion}
ev_dig <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = c(5e6, 8.91e5), evid = 1L,
             cmt = c("neut_tube", "bact_phagocytosed"), dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
             cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
)
sim_dig <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_vitro, ev_dig, returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L, omega = NA, sigma = NA)
ggplot(sim_dig, aes(time, log_cfu_intracellular)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Intracellular bacteria (log10 CFU/mL)",
       title = "Digestion of phagocytosed bacteria at 5 x 10^6 neutrophils/mL",
       caption = "Compare with the digestion panels of Figure 2a of Thorsted 2023.") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Bistable relation between neutrophils and bacterial burden

Figure 3b of the paper maps the change in bacterial burden after 1.5 h across
inocula and neutrophil concentrations. It shows that a neutrophil concentration
that clears a low inoculum fails against a high one. The grid below
reproduces that map.

```{r biphasic}
design3 <- tidyr::expand_grid(inoc = 10^(3:9), neut = 10^seq(5, 7.5, by = 0.25))
sim3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_vitro, invitro_events(design3, c(0, 1.5)),
                        returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L, omega = NA, sigma = NA) |>
  left_join(mutate(design3, id = row_number()), by = "id") |>
  group_by(id, inoc, neut) |>
  summarise(change = log_cfu[time == 1.5] - log_cfu[time == 0], .groups = "drop")

ggplot(sim3, aes(log10(neut), log10(inoc), fill = change)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "darkgreen", mid = "black", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(x = "Neutrophils (log10 cells/mL)", y = "Inoculum (log10 CFU/mL)",
       fill = "Change in\nlog10 CFU\nat 1.5 h",
       title = "Change in total viable CFU after 1.5 h",
       caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 3b of Thorsted 2023.") +
  theme_bw()

change_at <- function(n, b) sim3$change[abs(log10(sim3$neut) - n) < 1e-9 & abs(log10(sim3$inoc) - b) < 1e-9]
# Below Bmax, a higher inoculum fares no better at a fixed neutrophil
# concentration (the falling P/N term). At 10^9 CFU/mL the carrying capacity
# itself slows growth, so the comparison stops at 10^8.
chk3 <- sim3 |>
  dplyr::filter(inoc <= 1e8) |>
  group_by(neut) |>
  summarise(monotone = all(diff(change[order(inoc)]) >= -1e-6), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(
  all(chk3$monotone),
  # 10^6 neutrophils/mL clear inocula up to 10^6 CFU/mL but not 10^8 CFU/mL ...
  all(sapply(3:6, function(b) change_at(6, b)) < 0),
  change_at(6, 8) > 0,
  # ... which needs about ten times more neutrophils.
  change_at(7, 8) < 0
)
```

At a fixed neutrophil concentration the 1.5 h change rises with the inoculum,
because a growing ratio of phagocytosed bacteria to neutrophils slows both
phagocytosis and digestion. That matches the Discussion's reading of the
external data: about 0.5-1 x 10^6 neutrophils/mL contain inocula up to
10^6 CFU/mL, and larger inocula need progressively more neutrophils. The top
row (10^9 CFU/mL) changes less in every column because the burden is already
close to `Bmax`, which also slows growth in the controls.

## Closed-form checks from the Results and Discussion

At time zero no bacterium has been phagocytosed yet (`P/N = 0`) and the time
term is 1. The net first-order rate of the extracellular bacteria is then
`kgrowth - kdeath - kN,max * N / (N50,phag + N)`. In vivo the additional
capacity `kM,kill` is subtracted as well. The Discussion quotes the half-lives
this rate implies at the "critical neutrophil concentration" range of 0.3 and
0.5 x 10^6 cells/mL.

```{r closed-form}
p_v <- with(as.list(ui_vitro$theta), list(
  kgrowth = exp(lkgrowth), kdeath = exp(lkdeath), knmax = exp(lkn_max),
  n50 = exp(ln50_phag), pn50 = exp(lpn50), klag = exp(lklag)))
p_m <- with(as.list(ui_mouse$theta), list(
  kgrowth = exp(lkgrowth), kdeath = exp(lkdeath), knmax = exp(lkn_max),
  n50 = exp(ln50_phag), kmkill = exp(lkm_kill), kmloss = exp(lkm_loss)))
net_vitro <- function(n) p_v$kgrowth - p_v$kdeath - p_v$knmax * n / (p_v$n50 + n)
net_mouse <- function(n) p_m$kgrowth - p_m$kdeath - p_m$knmax * n / (p_m$n50 + n) - p_m$kmkill

cf <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~published, ~model,
  "In vitro doubling time (h)", 0.377, log(2) / p_v$kgrowth,
  "klag half-life (h)", 2.39, log(2) / p_v$klag,
  "In vitro initial bacterial half-life at 0.3 x 10^6 N/mL (h)", 5.73, -log(2) / net_vitro(0.3e6),
  "In vitro initial bacterial half-life at 0.5 x 10^6 N/mL (h)", 0.724, -log(2) / net_vitro(0.5e6),
  "In vivo initial bacterial half-life at 0.3 x 10^6 N/mL (h)", 5.72, -log(2) / net_mouse(0.3e6),
  "In vivo initial bacterial half-life at 0.5 x 10^6 N/mL (h)", 3.49, -log(2) / net_mouse(0.5e6),
  "In vivo doubling time (h)", 1.38, log(2) / p_m$kgrowth,
  "kN,max half-life in vivo (h)", 0.845, log(2) / p_m$knmax,
  "kM,kill half-life, immune-competent (h)", 2.42, log(2) / p_m$kmkill,
  "kM,loss half-life (h)", 62, log(2) / p_m$kmloss,
  "Rate reduction at 50 CFU per neutrophil (%)", 94, 100 * 50 / (50 + p_v$pn50)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - published) / published)
cf |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Published" = published, "Model" = model,
                "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # Quantities that depend only on in vitro estimates reproduce to rounding.
  all(abs(cf$pct_diff[c(1:4, 7:11)]) < 1.5),
  # The two in vivo initial half-lives are a small difference of large rates,
  # so the 0.502 1/h rounding of kgrowth moves them by several percent.
  all(abs(cf$pct_diff[5:6]) < 10)
)
```

The in vitro quantities match the paper to its printed precision. The two in
vivo initial half-lives come out 4-6% shorter than the Discussion quotes. Both
quoted values imply the same net growth rate, which is what an in vivo
`kgrowth` of about 0.510 1/h would give against the 0.502 1/h in Table 2. A
net rate close to zero amplifies that 1.6% difference in `kgrowth`.

# Mouse behaviour

## Cyclophosphamide pharmacokinetics (PKNCA)

The cyclophosphamide layer is a one-compartment model with first-order
absorption, scaled from rats and fixed. PKNCA on a single 50 mg/kg dose
(1.25 mg in a 25 g mouse) should recover `AUC = dose / CL` and the terminal
half-life `log(2) / (CL / V)`, because absorption (`ka` = 20.9 1/h) is ten
times faster than elimination.

```{r cp-pk}
ev_cp <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 1.25, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, seq(0.02, 0.5, by = 0.02), seq(0.6, 6, by = 0.1)),
             amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
)
sim_cp <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_mouse, ev_cp, returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L, omega = NA, sigma = NA) |>
  mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "50 mg/kg IP")

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(dplyr::filter(sim_cp, !is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(data.frame(id = 1L, treatment = "50 mg/kg IP", time = 0, amt = 1.25),
                             amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca$result)

cl_cp <- exp(ui_mouse$theta[["lcl"]])
v_cp <- exp(ui_mouse$theta[["lvc"]])
ref_cp <- data.frame(
  treatment = "50 mg/kg IP",
  aucinf.obs = 1.25 / cl_cp,
  half.life = log(2) / (cl_cp / v_cp)
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_tbl,
  reference = ref_cp,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/mL", half.life = "h")
) |>
  knitr::kable()

chk_cp <- nca_tbl |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life"))
stopifnot(
  abs(chk_cp$PPORRES[chk_cp$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"] / ref_cp$aucinf.obs - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(chk_cp$PPORRES[chk_cp$PPTESTCD == "half.life"] / ref_cp$half.life - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The reference column is the closed form from the fixed `CL` and `V`. The paper
reports no NCA for cyclophosphamide.

## Steady state without drug or bacteria

With neither cyclophosphamide nor bacteria, every neutrophil pool should stay
at `Ncirc,T0`. Lung neutrophils per lung then equal `0.175 x Ncirc,T0`.

```{r steady-state}
ev_ss <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 24, 168, 500), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
                    cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_mouse, ev_ss, returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L, omega = NA, sigma = NA)
circ0 <- exp(ui_mouse$theta[["lcirc0"]])
stopifnot(
  all(abs(sim_ss$circ / circ0 - 1) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(sim_ss$neut_lung / circ0 - 1) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(sim_ss$log_neut_lung - log10(0.175 * circ0)) < 1e-6)
)
sim_ss[, c("time", "circ", "neut_lung", "log_anc", "log_neut_lung")]
```

## Mice-2: cyclophosphamide pretreatment and infection

Mice-2 gave cyclophosphamide 96 and 24 h before inoculation, at model times 0
and 72 h, and inoculated 1.57 x 10^7 CFU/g lung at 96 h. Doses are in mg for a
25 g mouse. The surge in lung neutrophil influx and the decay of the
additional phagocytic capacity both run from the first bacterial dose into
`bact_susceptible`.

```{r mice2}
regimens <- data.frame(
  regimen = factor(c("Vehicle", "50/50 mg/kg", "100/50 mg/kg", "200/150 mg/kg"),
                   levels = c("Vehicle", "50/50 mg/kg", "100/50 mg/kg", "200/150 mg/kg")),
  d1 = c(0, 50, 100, 200), d2 = c(0, 50, 50, 150)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev_m2 <- bind_rows(
  regimens |>
    dplyr::filter(d1 > 0) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(d1, d2), names_to = "dose", values_to = "mgkg") |>
    transmute(id, time = ifelse(dose == "d1", 0, 72), amt = mgkg * 0.025, evid = 1L,
              cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = regimens$id, time = 96, amt = 1.567e7, evid = 1L,
             cmt = "bact_susceptible", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = regimens$id, time = seq(0, 168, by = 1)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_m2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_mouse, ev_m2, returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L, omega = NA, sigma = NA) |>
  left_join(regimens[, c("id", "regimen")], by = "id")

obs_m2 <- s1_obs |>
  dplyr::filter(STUD == 130) |>
  mutate(regimen = regimens$regimen[ID - 1300],
         panel = ifelse(LOCA == 5, "Blood neutrophils (log10 cells/mL)", "Lung CFU (log10 CFU/g)"))

sim_m2_long <- sim_m2 |>
  dplyr::select(time, regimen, log_anc, log_cfu) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(log_anc, log_cfu), names_to = "out", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(panel = ifelse(out == "log_anc", "Blood neutrophils (log10 cells/mL)", "Lung CFU (log10 CFU/g)")) |>
  dplyr::filter(out == "log_anc" | time >= 96)

ggplot(sim_m2_long, aes(time, value, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = obs_m2, aes(TIME, DV, colour = regimen)) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time since first cyclophosphamide dose (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Mice-2: cyclophosphamide pretreatment, inoculation at 96 h",
       caption = "Lines: packaged model. Points: Table S1. Compare with Figure 2b-c of Thorsted 2023.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Deeper pretreatment leaves fewer neutrophils at inoculation and more bacteria
# 24 h later.
at96 <- sim_m2 |> dplyr::filter(time == 96) |> arrange(regimen)
at120 <- sim_m2 |> dplyr::filter(time == 120) |> arrange(regimen)
stopifnot(
  all(diff(at96$log_anc) < 0),
  all(diff(at120$log_cfu) > 0)
)
```

## Immune-competent mice: lung neutrophil surge and clearance

The three inocula of Mice-3 (5.71 x 10^6 to 5.71 x 10^8 CFU/g lung) in mice
without cyclophosphamide.

```{r competent}
inocs <- c(5.71e6, 5.71e7, 5.71e8)
ev_ic <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_along(inocs), time = 0, amt = inocs, evid = 1L,
             cmt = "bact_susceptible", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_along(inocs), time = seq(0, 168, by = 1)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_ic <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_mouse, ev_ic, returnType = "data.frame", cores = 1L, omega = NA, sigma = NA) |>
  mutate(inoculum = factor(format(inocs[id], scientific = TRUE)))

ggplot(sim_ic, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = inoculum)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(s1_obs, STUD %in% c(100, 200), LOCA == 4),
             aes(TIME, DV), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey30") +
  labs(x = "Time after inoculation (h)", y = "Lung bacteria (log10 CFU/g)",
       colour = "Inoculum (CFU/g)",
       title = "Immune-competent mice",
       caption = "Points: Mice-1 and Mice-3 records from Table S1. Compare with Figure 2c of Thorsted 2023.") +
  theme_bw()

ggplot(dplyr::filter(sim_ic, id == 1), aes(time, log_neut_lung)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(s1_obs, STUD == 230, LOCA == 7), aes(TIME, DV),
             inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Time after inoculation (h)", y = "Lung neutrophils (log10 cells/lung)",
       title = "Post-inoculation neutrophil influx into the lung",
       caption = "Points: Mice-4 records from Table S1. Compare with Figure 2b of Thorsted 2023.") +
  theme_bw()

peak <- sim_ic |> dplyr::filter(id == 1) |> slice_max(neut_lung, n = 1)
peak[, c("time", "neut_lung")]
stopifnot(
  # Discussion: the lung neutrophil concentration exceeded 6.31 x 10^7 cells/g,
  # more than 30 times the circulating concentration, about 2 days after
  # inoculation.
  peak$neut_lung > 6.31e7,
  peak$neut_lung / circ0 > 30,
  peak$time > 48, peak$time < 72,
  # All immune-competent mice clear even the highest inoculum.
  all(sim_ic$log_cfu[sim_ic$time == 168] < log10(inocs) - 4)
)
```

# Simulations not reproduced

Figures 4 and 5 project neutrophil and bacterial time courses in 1000 patients
of 70 kg on three cyclophosphamide regimens, with bacteria deposited on day 35.
They use a published population PK model of cyclophosphamide in cancer
patients (Sandstrom 2006, reference 42) with between-subject variability on
`Ncirc,T0`, `MTT`, `CL`, `V` and the drug effect. The paper prints neither the
human cyclophosphamide PK parameters nor the human values of the neutrophil
system parameters. The mouse model therefore cannot reproduce those figures,
and they are not attempted here.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two files for one simultaneous fit.** The authors estimated the in vitro
  and in vivo parameters together. The library splits them by experimental
  system. The parameters shared across systems (`kdeath`, `Bmax`, `N50,dig`,
  `N50,phag`, `P/N50`) carry the same Table 2 value in both files. The
  system-specific values (`kgrowth`, `kN,max`, `kN,loss`) are the Table 2 in
  vitro and in vivo rows. Data S2 writes the in vivo `kgrowth` and `kN,max` as
  in vitro estimate times multiplier, and Table 2 reports the products.
* **Mice-4 growth multiplier omitted.** Data S2 estimates a separate in vivo
  growth multiplier for Mice-4 alone (`THETA(25)`), but no value for it
  appears in Table 2 or the text. The mouse model applies the common in vivo
  `kgrowth` (0.502 1/h) to every infection. Its Mice-4 CFU predictions are
  therefore too high (see the deposited-data check above).
* **Macrophage compartment omitted.** Data S2 also carries a lung macrophage
  turnover compartment (`MLUNG`, `THETA(16)` to `THETA(20)`, all fixed). It
  feeds no other equation. The additional phagocytic capacity scales with
  circulating neutrophils (`MACRF = CIRC / 10**NEU0`), not with this
  compartment. The paper reports that no link to the macrophage time course
  could be established and counts no macrophage observations in its data
  summary. Leaving the compartment out changes none of the fitted outputs.
* **Time since inoculation.** Data S2 shifts time by `EXTRT` (96 h for Mice-2,
  0 otherwise) in the surge centre `NT0` and in the `kM,loss` decay. It
  switches the surge off for experiments without an inoculum (`INOC = 0`). The
  mouse model measures both from the first bacterial dose into
  `bact_susceptible` (`tafd()`) and keeps the surge off until that dose.
  The two forms agree whenever bacteria are inoculated at time 0, which
  covers every study except Mice-2. Data S2's surge is a bell curve in time, so
  for Mice-2 it already starts to rise about a day before the 96 h inoculation
  and reaches 1.3 at the inoculation itself. Re-solving Mice-2 (vehicle arm)
  with the Data S2 form gives 1.65-fold more lung neutrophils at inoculation
  (2.78 vs 1.69 x 10^6 cells/g) and 0.18 log10 fewer CFU/g at 120 h (4.98 vs
  5.16). The library form needs no inoculation-time covariate and does not
  raise lung neutrophils before infection.
* **A merged line in Data S2.** In the supplement as published, the statement
  `IF(STUD > 99) MKNA = THETA(6) * THETA(24)` sits on the same line as the
  comment of the preceding `MKNK` statement. Read literally, that would comment
  it out. Table 2 nevertheless reports an estimated `kM,loss` of 0.0111 1/h
  (RSE 45%), which the Discussion converts to a 62 h half-life. The model
  therefore treats it as a separate statement, with `kM,loss` taken directly
  from Table 2.
* **Allometric exponent for MTT.** The Methods text says MTT was scaled with
  an exponent of 0.25. Data S2 uses 0.136 (`MTT = 52.8 * (0.025/0.295)**0.136`),
  and only 0.136 reproduces the 37.7 h in Table 2. The model follows Data S2.
* **Study labels.** The `STUD` comments in Data S2 attach Leijh 1980 to study 3
  and Leijh 1979 to study 4, whereas Table 1 cites them the other way round.
  The data themselves are consistent with the model: the experiments whose
  inoculum is dosed into the phagocytosed compartment report intracellular CFU.
* **Shared residual SDs.** Data S2 uses one residual SD for every in vitro CFU
  measurement type and one for blood and lung neutrophils. nlmixr2 needs one
  residual parameter per endpoint, so each shared estimate appears under
  several names with the same value.
* **Single-threaded solves.** Every `rxSolve()` call here passes
  `cores = 1L`. With the default thread count, rxode2 5.1.8 sometimes
  returned a falling neutrophil count for an untreated mouse (Mice-3, highest
  inoculum) when that mouse was solved in the same event table as the
  cyclophosphamide-treated Mice-2 animals. Single-threaded solves were
  identical on every repeat. Multi-subject simulations of the mouse model
  should use `cores = 1L` until that behaviour is resolved.
* **log10 floor.** Data S2 sets non-positive extracellular and total CFU to 1
  before the log10. The models do the same, and apply the same floor to the
  intracellular output, which Data S2 left unguarded.
